title: Set up accounting
summary: Choose accounting software and configure the chart of accounts so the books can close every month.

parts.title: Compare accounting tools
parts.guidance: Compare accounting tools for the entities, currencies, reporting basis, tax outputs, invoice volume, payroll and integrations the company needs. Include the accountant and bookkeeper’s requirements for permissions, audit history and exports. Test representative transactions and reports, then identify any statutory or specialist work that remains outside the software before choosing the service.

parts.title: Sign up and configure the chart of accounts
parts.guidance: Configure the entity, reporting basis, financial year and opening balances with the accountant. Build a chart of accounts that supports the company’s transactions and required reports, avoiding overlapping categories. Set appropriate administrator and reviewer access and test representative postings and reports. Use the local route to resolve statutory requirements before relying on the configuration for live books.

options.title: Default — Sign up and configure the chart of accounts
options.summary: Set the company’s chart of accounts, reporting year, currencies and access roles in the selected workspace. Map opening balances and recurring transactions to the chart with the accountant. Establish consistent treatments for revenue, payroll, tax, capital and transfers, and check a trial report before importing the full history.

options.title: India - Companies Act books + audit
options.summary: Agree the applicable Indian reporting framework, books and audit arrangements with the accountant for the company’s actual form and circumstances. Configure ledger categories, tax mappings, record retention and reporting outputs accordingly. Distinguish bookkeeping and any required independent review, and test a sample period to see whether the system produces the needed accounts.
options.when: Setting up the books in India

options.title: UK - FRS 105/102 + statutory accounts
options.summary: Establish the UK accounting standard and reporting options that apply, including support for any small-company or micro-entity treatment. Configure the chart, year end and accounts outputs with the accountant and reconcile opening balances. Check a sample package against the statutory accounts and tax work, identifying audit work and other tasks that need separate handling.
options.when: Setting up the books in the United Kingdom

options.title: Germany - GoBD books + SKR03/04
options.summary: Agree the German chart of accounts and bookkeeping workflow with the tax adviser, including invoice handling, corrections, exports and retention. Test traceability from source documents through postings and reports, including structured invoices, against the applicable GoBD requirements. Address gaps in the software or operating procedure before importing the company’s history.
options.when: Setting up the books in Germany

options.title: France - Plan Comptable General + FEC
options.summary: Map the French company’s transactions to the applicable accounting plan and reports with its accountant. Check source-document retention, posting history and FEC export support. Generate a sample FEC and reconcile its structure and contents to the ledger, correcting gaps in the setup before live records depend on it.
options.when: Setting up the books in France

parts.title: Connect bank and card feeds
parts.guidance: List bank and card accounts by accounting entity and agree the import start date with the bookkeeper. The authorized account administrator connects each feed to the right ledger account. Detect overlap with manual imports and reconcile sample transactions and opening balances to statements. Set up follow-up for failed feeds so later books remain complete.

verify.how: Bank and card transactions import into the ledger within a day of connecting.

geoNotes.summary: Books follow the Companies Act and Indian accounting standards, and — unlike everywhere else — EVERY company needs a statutory audit by a chartered accountant from year one, so the auditor relationship starts with the books.
Statutory accounts for Companies House are unavoidable, but most startups qualify for the small-company audit exemption; FRS 105/102 set the accounting framework your software must map to.

Bookkeeping must be GoBD-compliant (tamper-evident, German retention rules), the de-facto chart of accounts is DATEV's SKR03/SKR04, and nearly every startup runs the books through a Steuerberater who files via ELSTER.
France mandates the chart of accounts: the Plan Comptable Général from the ANC is law, and the tax authority can demand your ledger as a standardized FEC file — accounting software must speak both.

metadata.supportReason: Choosing and configuring the software is guided form work; connecting bank and card feeds runs on the accounting APIs.
